summary: Linguist Thomas Sebeok studied at Fasori Gimnázium, Magdalene College, the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield, and Princeton University under Roman Jakobson. He was a Distinguished Professor Emeritus at Indiana University Bloomington, where he served from 1943 to 1991.
Active in Indology and archaeology, Thomas Seymour Burt studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1821 to 1823. He served as a Major in the Bengal Engineers from 1824 to 1847.

Thomas Walker Arnold studied at Magdalene College under Edward Byles Cowell. He held posts at Aligarh Muslim University, Government College University, Lahore, the University of the Punjab, the India Office, and SOAS University of London as Professor of Arabic and Islamic Studies.
Thomas Watters worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Queen's University Belfast and Queen's University of Ireland before serving in HM Diplomatic Service from 1863 to 1895.

Thomas Welbourne Clark studied at Nottingham, Cambridge, and SOAS under Cyril Alexander Rylands, Ralph Lilley Turner, and Walter Sutton Page. Working in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at SOAS from 1948 and visited the University of Pennsylvania in 1961.

Historian Thomas Wolseley Haig studied at Wellington College and Sandhurst. He served in the Indian Civil Service, as Lecturer in Persian at SOAS (1923-1938), and as Professor of Arabic, Persian and Hindustani at Trinity College, Hartford (1924-1925).
Thomas Zehnder, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned his PhD at the University of Zurich under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang studied at the University of Nanking under John Dewey and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Active in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he taught at National Central University (1925-1948) and National Taiwan University (1948-1973).

Thubten Chodron studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery under several teachers, including Thubten Yeshe. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, she held posts in Italy and Singapore before founding and leading Sravasti Abbey as abbess.

Scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies Thubten Jigme Norbu studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965-1992).
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. He was a teacher to the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, Dagpo Rinpoche, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.
Thubten Samphel studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and Columbia University. He worked in the field of Tibetology and served at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar Thubten Yeshe studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Rabten, Trijang Rinpoche, and Zong Rinpoche. He founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, and taught at the University of California, Santa Cruz (1977-1978).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche studied under Geshe Rabten and Thubten Yeshe, among others. He co-founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, where he served as spiritual director from 1984, working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology.

Thupten Jinpa studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and the University of Cambridge. Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he held positions at Ganden Monastery, Girton College, the Institute of Tibetan Classics, and Stanford University.
Working in the fields of computational studies and Tibetology, Thupten Tsering has held academic posts at Tibet University and the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.
Thushini S. Jayawardena is a scholar of religious studies who completed a PhD at Auckland University of Technology in 2017 and studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka.

Théodore Pavie studied under Eugène Burnouf and Garcin de Tassy. A scholar of Indology and sinology, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852-1857) and taught at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Thích Minh Châu earned his PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He was a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1953-1961) and served as Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (1964-1975).
A scholar in the field of Buddhist studies, Thích Thiện Châu pursued higher education at Paris-Sorbonne University and completed a doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1977.
